extracted.intended_audience: heads of executive departments and establishments; agency ADP/procurement managers and policy officials
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for federal agencies on implementing OMB Circular A-76 for automatic data processing (ADP) requirements, including when to contract ADP services, how to perform cost comparisons, planning and termination procedures, and required agency actions and submissions to OMB/GSA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy preference for commercial ADP services
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies will obtain ADP services from competitive commercial sources in preference to direct operation of in-house activities, consistent with the Government's general policy of reliance on the private sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The service approach (contractor performs the service) is preferred over government ownership/operation of ADP facilities. Agencies should move toward greater use of commercial ADP services in lieu of government ownership and operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability scope
rubrics_metrics.description: This Transmittal Memorandum is applicable to all general purpose data processing activities operated and managed by executive agencies that provide services that are obtainable from a private source, as defined in Circular No. A-76.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an activity meets the Circular No. A-76 definition of a commercial or industrial activity, it is subject to the requirements of the Circular, including review requirements for new starts, expansions, upgrades, replacements, or modernizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: New-start and change-review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All Government ADP activities that meet the Circular No. A-76 definition of a commercial or industrial activity are subject to a 'new start' review for initiation, expansion, upgrade, replacement, or modernization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum emphasis should be placed on reviewing new starts to avoid investment and financial commitments for ADP activities that have not been reviewed and justified under Circular No. A-76.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible exceptions to contracting-out policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptions are allowed if fully reviewed and documented in cases such as: commercial services would disrupt or delay accomplishment of mission; combat support; no commercial source available; service is available from another Federal Agency; commercial service will cost more (requires detailed cost analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classified status or mission-related classification alone is not an adequate reason for exception. When invoking 'commercial service will cost more', agencies must follow elaborate cost study instructions and fully document justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency planning and management program elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency must initiate a positive action program to implement the policy; program elements include revision of agency instructions and directives, emphasis on new starts review, preparation of a multiyear ADP plan, and development of a program outline with milestones and targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: (a) review and revise agency instructions to incorporate Circular No. A-76 requirements early in ADP system planning; (b) prepare a multiyear plan (to be included in the Spring ADP Plan) projecting requirements and schedules to increase private-sector reliance; (c) set goals and use Management by Objective (MBO) where appropriate; (d) develop a program outline with milestones/targets for submission to OMB within ninety days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express requirements in service terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Government ADP requirements normally will be expressed in terms of the services to be performed, rather than the equipment and software to be used in performing these services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements of requirements should allow the contractor maximum flexibility in type of equipment and personnel used, as long as satisfactory services are provided. This avoids prescribing specific hardware/software solutions and favors outcome-based specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of equipment-rental-as-policy workaround
rubrics_metrics.description: Renting or buying equipment and having private contractors operate the equipment is not considered responsive to the policy of relying on commercial services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preferred model is contracting for services (contractor performs the ADP service); simply contracting operators to run government-owned equipment does not meet the intent of Circular A-76.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of in-house expertise for oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: The service approach does not eliminate the need for in-house expertise; agencies should maintain enough technical staff to prepare service performance specifications and to monitor contractor performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should retain capability for system design, specification writing, and contractor oversight, but reduce the level of in-house operational staff to that necessary for management and monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: GSA delegation request documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency requests to GSA for delegation of procurement authority for acquisition of ADP equipment to be operated by the agency must include a specific statement indicating the proposed acquisition has been reviewed and approved under the provisions of Circular No. A-76, or an explanation of why the Circular does not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests lacking this statement must explain why A-76 is inapplicable; documentation is required to ensure procurement authority decisions reflect A-76 policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on when to perform cost studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies to determine whether a commercial or industrial ADP activity can be justified on the basis of cost should be limited to situations where there is reason to assume that in-house costs might be significantly less than competitive commercial prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not perform exhaustive cost studies indiscriminately; focus cost studies where initial indicators suggest in-house performance could be cheaper. When cost studies are made, include all cost elements specified in Circular No. A-76.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost differential to favor commercial services (risk adjustment)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost differential favoring reliance on commercial sources should reflect the possibility of early obsolescence and uncertainty of requirements; Circular No. A-76 specifies the differential should normally be at least 10% for any new start, and for ADP activities this differential can be substantially more than 10%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set the differential for each cost study at a level appropriate to the degree of risk and uncertainty involved in Government operation of the particular activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements required in equitable and accurate cost comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: In preparing cost comparisons particular attention must be given to: (1) determination of a valid commercial cost figure (generally requires solicitation of competitive bids); (2) Government and commercial cost estimates must be based on equivalent services; (3) fair market value of equipment/facilities that would become excess must be included as a Government cost; (4) proper residual/salvage value of equipment proposed for acquisition must be determined to ensure correct depreciation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure equivalence of service scope between government and commercial estimates; solicit objective commercial proposals; include market value offsets and correct depreciation/residual assumptions in Government cost figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Circular A-76 cost elements interim guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: More comprehensive guidance is being developed to assist agencies in calculating both Government and commercial costs; in the interim, guidance available in Circular No. A-76 and this Memorandum will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must follow A-76 cost element prescriptions now, and apply interim guidance here until more detailed instructions are issued by OMB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency ADP activity review and termination planning
rubrics_metrics.description: All agency ADP activities should be reviewed by September 30, 1977 to determine whether Government performance is justified under the exception criteria of Circular No. A-76. When a Government commercial or industrial activity is to be terminated or reduced, the action must be carefully planned to ensure transition without disruption of vital services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planning should include workforce considerations, phased reductions, and coordination with incoming contract services to include overlap periods when necessary to avoid mission disruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration for displaced Government employees
rubrics_metrics.description: When terminating or curtailing Government ADP activities, agencies must give all reasonable consideration for Government employees displaced, including phased reduction of operations to facilitate reassignment and reduction by attrition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement personnel transition plans (reassignment, attrition, phased reductions) to mitigate workforce impacts and enable orderly transitions to commercial services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract transition coordination to avoid mission disruption
rubrics_metrics.description: Careful coordination of contract services, including a period of overlap when necessary, is required to avoid disruption of the agency mission during conversion to commercial ADP services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan contract start/stop dates and overlap periods so that vital services are continuously provided during handover from government operation to contractor performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of multiyear ADP plans to OMB
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare and submit to OMB annual multiyear ADP plans (beginning with 1977 submission) projecting new and continuing ADP requirements and including schedules of actions to achieve greater reliance on the private sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include milestones, targets, and where appropriate goals using MBO methodology. Use these plans to document agency strategies for increased commercial reliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and submit program outline with milestones within 90 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should develop a program outline for achieving greater reliance on commercial services, with milestones and specific targets for submission to OMB within ninety days from issuance of this Transmittal Memorandum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The outline should set concrete milestones and targets and be suitable for oversight and monitoring by OMB as part of the agency's compliance with Circular A-76.
